clue.text: Planet above the horizon: it appears between start and end of June, right?

indicators.note: appears between says the following letters sit between the two letters taken from June
start and end of picks the first and last letters of the word June

parts.note: something above the horizon is up, as the sun is up

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes a planet rising into view between early and late June.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system, an example of the category named.

clue.text: American novelist gets stuck penning English

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep are penned, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a machine that gets stuck jams

explanation.surface: A US author hits writer's block while trying to write in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist, author of The Portrait of a Lady.

clue.text: Staff not heartless with a fried meal

parts.note: a staff is a pole or rod

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word not is removed

parts.note: the a is taken as written, with joining it on

explanation.surface: A dish of fried food is served without the usual walking stick, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is Italian maize meal, often set and then fried in slices.

clue.text: Quality surrounds good university offering no clear results? Unable to say

indicators.note: surrounds says the first piece wraps round the next ones

parts.note: the tone of something is its quality or character
a tied match produces no clear winner

explanation.surface: A good university's research is inconclusive and its spokesman cannot comment.
explanation.walkthrough: TONE surrounds G and U to give TONGUE; a tie is a contest with no clear result.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tongue-tied is too shy or confused to speak, so unable to say anything.

clue.text: Architects initially linked to dull coarse humour

parts.note: RIBA is the Royal Institute of British Architects, the UK architects' professional body

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word linked

parts.note: dry means dull or uninteresting; to joins it on

explanation.surface: Architects are blamed early on for crude, boring jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Architects initially' looks like one instruction; it is RIBA, and 'initially' acts on 'linked' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is vulgar, bawdy joking, which is coarse humour by another name.

clue.text: Rejected support? Left involved in first-class foul-up

indicators.note: rejected suggests turning back, so the word for support is read backwards

parts.note: a bed is a support, as for a machine or plants

indicators.note: involved in says one letter goes inside the word for first-class

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-class

explanation.surface: Political backing withdrawn and the Left caught up in a top-level mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure, which is a foul-up in casual speech.

clue.text: Day and year around simple vessel affected by currents around Florida

indicators.note: around says the two letters sit either side of the vessel

parts.note: a raft is the simplest sort of boat

explanation.surface: A raft drifts for days and years, pushed by the currents off Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around Florida' marks the American spelling: in Britain the word is spelt draughty.
explanation.definitionFit: A drafty room is one with cold air currents through it, in the US spelling.

clue.text: Runs from close encounter in part of shrubbery

indicators.note: Runs from means that letter leaves the word for close encounter

parts.note: a brush, as a brush with death, is a close encounter
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees a near miss by hiding in the shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is planted with shrubs, and a single shrub is one component of it.

clue.text: Rogue cuddling 12: one account of the heart

indicators.note: cuddling means hugging, so the word for rogue wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a cad is a rogue or bounder
12 across is KING, abbreviated R, from Latin rex
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rascal cosies up to the monarch, one tale of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to KING, which gives R (rex).
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective meaning relating to the heart.

clue.text: Durable work unit about to come in still

indicators.note: to come in says the following letters enter the word for still

parts.note: still water is even, calm and flat
the erg is a unit of work in physics
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A long-lasting job is about to come in, still.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen stays fresh and popular for years, so it is long-lasting.

clue.text: Some Londoners (but only some) will produce fruit

indicators.note: but only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few Londoners will grow fruit, though not many.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit, so the word stands for fruit as an example.

clue.text: Café supporter I placed nearer the rear

indicators.note: placed nearer the rear says the letter I moves one step towards the end of the word

parts.note: a brassiere, or bra, is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A café fan explains where he sat himself, towards the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the I in BRASSIERE one place along, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant or café serving simple food.

clue.text: Easy in lust, possibly displaying this?

definitions.text: Easy in lust, possibly displaying this?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed about desire shows a fleshly side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a person easy in lust may well show it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensuality is indulgence in physical pleasure, what someone at ease with lust displays.

clue.text: Family ruling ultimately produces me?

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word ruling

explanation.surface: A monarch muses that a ruling dynasty eventually produces him.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes hereditary monarchy: the royal family in power ends up producing the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is born of a ruling dynasty, so the speaker is a hereditary sovereign.

clue.text: Price arranged with Mafia regarding usable evidence?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A price fixed with the Mafia, which a court might hear about.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima facie evidence is enough on first sight to establish a fact unless rebutted.

clue.text: Slovenly woman most recently opening tin

indicators.note: opening says the first word is opened up to take the other inside

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
latter means the last-mentioned or nearest in time, so most recent

explanation.surface: An untidy woman has lately taken to opening cans.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old, unkind term for a dirty, untidy woman.

clue.text: Components of antimony most unlikely in work on cleaning stone

parts.note: the chemical symbol for antimony is Sb, whose components are S and B
the last person to do something is the most unlikely one to do it

explanation.surface: Antimony compounds are rarely used to clean stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandblasting cleans masonry by firing grit at it under air pressure.

clue.text: Source of information over length involved in marathon?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: involved in says the letter goes inside the word for marathon

parts.note: a marathon is a long running race

explanation.surface: A runner wants to know how long the marathon course is.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person or shrine consulted for authoritative knowledge or prophecy.

clue.text: Writer's beset by former partners — alimony, child support, etc?

indicators.note: beset by says the word for writer's is surrounded by the following word

parts.note: exes are former spouses or partners
a pen is a writer, so the writer's is pen's

explanation.surface: An author is hounded by ex-wives for maintenance money.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony and child support are costs one must pay out, so outgoings or expenses.

clue.text: Crazy getting married, say, for the spicy stuff

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
eg means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: Going mad about marriage in exchange for something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is a spice ground from the seed of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Difficult police operation after half of team wiped out

indicators.note: after says the police operation piece comes later in the answer than the half of team
half of keeps only the first two of the four letters of team

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: A tough police raid after half the squad was eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiped out' adds to 'half of': the back half of team is lost, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A testing task is a demanding one, which puts you to the test.

clue.text: Old fool carrying axes? It sends mixed messages

indicators.note: carrying says the pieces either side hold the axes letters inside

parts.note: a moron is a fool
X and Y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: An elderly idiot wielding axes is a confusing sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech joining contradictory terms, such as deafening silence, says two opposed things.

clue.text: Carrier I found cast in curious metal

indicators.note: cast in means put inside, as letters thrown into another word

parts.note: rum means odd or curious, in old British slang
a hod is a builder's carrier for bricks

explanation.surface: A builder's hod turns out to have been cast in an odd metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests an anagram, but HOD and I go in unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a hard silvery element of the platinum group, a metal.

clue.text: Fancily-dressed folk around street: what will aid the paparazzi?

indicators.note: around says these letters surround the abbreviation for street

parts.note: fops are men too concerned with fine clothes

explanation.surface: Dandies gathering in the street are a gift for photographers.
explanation.definitionFit: F-stops are camera aperture settings, used by any photographer, paparazzi included.

clue.text: 27 browses every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means taking letters at intervals, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: The head of the company occasionally looks round the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is CHIEF, the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person in charge, a chief in another word.

clue.text: Part of London Fields — go so wild here

indicators.note: wild suggests these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: London Fields, a park in Hackney, is where people get rowdy.
explanation.walkthrough: London Fields is a park in east London; 'London' is borrowed from it for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is the peninsula in east London that holds Canary Wharf.

clue.text: Seat the ultimate in glamour till now

parts.note: a sofa is a seat for several people

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the last letter of the word glamour

explanation.surface: This couch is the last word in glamour, up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is an idiom meaning up to the present moment.

clue.text: Nobleman expected to throttle 12

indicators.note: to throttle means to grip round the neck, so this word goes round the next letter

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
12 across is KING, abbreviated K, as in chess

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is expected to strangle the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, a nobleman.

clue.text: Bitter detectives entering area beginning to uncover corrupt soul

indicators.note: entering says the detectives go inside the string built from area, uncover and soul
beginning to picks the first letter of the word uncover
corrupt means spoiled, so the letters of soul are mixed up

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

explanation.surface: Detectives arrive to expose a corrupt person's sour secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' turns SOUL into LOUS, giving AULOUS; 'entering' puts CID inside that, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidulous means sharp or sour in taste or manner, so bitter.

clue.text: Hurry to interrupt returning soccer club 22

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into the reversed club letters
returning says the abbreviation for a football club is read backwards

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club
hie is an old word meaning hurry

explanation.surface: A manager rushes to break up the returning soccer team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns FC into CF; 22 across is BOSS, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is a leader or head, another word for a boss.

clue.text: Time to take another line, heading away from dangerous animal

indicators.note: heading away says the first letter of the word for take another line goes

parts.note: to digress is to wander off onto another topic

explanation.surface: Time to change course and get away from a dangerous beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, a big cat and a dangerous predator.

clue.text: One heats up players in series

indicators.note: in says the players go inside the abbreviation for series

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Players warming up during a series of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a pan or device that cooks or warms food by steam.
